showHistory.title: For Parents and Children
showHistory.body: Lord, we pray for parents carrying heavy responsibilities and for children trying to find their way. Give wisdom where words are hard, and gentleness where hearts are tender. Let our homes be places of safety and grace. Amen.

showHistory.title: Counting Gifts
showHistory.body: Lord, we stop to name what is good in this day, even if it is only one thing. Thank You for kindness shown to us and for the chance to show kindness to someone else. Amen.

showHistory.title: A Word for Today
showHistory.body: But they that wait upon the Lord shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; and they shall walk, and not faint.

showHistory.title: Proverbs 3:5 (KJV)
showHistory.body: Understanding has limits. Trust reaches further than what we can figure out.

showHistory.title: A Thankful Heart
showHistory.body: Father, thank You for the small things we often forget to notice: a meal, a friend’s voice, a moment of quiet. Teach us to receive today with open hands. Let gratitude shape the way we speak to one another. Amen.

showHistory.title: A Word for Today
showHistory.body: Cast thy burden upon the Lord, and he shall sustain thee: he shall never suffer the righteous to be moved.

showHistory.title: Our Community in Prayer
showHistory.body: As we pray together, let us remember that we are not alone. If you are praying for someone today, you are part of something larger than this screen. Let us hold one another with hope.

showHistory.title: Strength for the Weary
showHistory.body: Lord, we pray for everyone who is tired in a way that sleep does not fix. Renew their strength from the inside out. Give them one clear step for today and the grace to keep going. Amen.

showHistory.title: A Word for Today
showHistory.body: And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose.

showHistory.title: When the Body Is Weak
showHistory.body: God of all comfort, You know the pain that words cannot carry. We ask for Your presence to be felt in hospital rooms, at home, and in quiet hours. Sustain the weary, and remind them that they are deeply loved. Amen.
